'''''Cenchrus alopecuroides''''', previously '''''Pennisetum alopecuroides''''' (Pen-ih-SEE-tum al-oh-pek-yur-OY-deez),<ref>{{cite web|title=Pennisetum alopecuroides - Fountain Grass|url=http://www.bluestem.ca/pennisetum-alopec.htm|website=Bluestem|accessdate=10 November 2016}}</ref> commonly known as the '''Chinese pennisetum''', '''Chinese fountaingrass''', '''dwarf fountain grass''', '''foxtail fountain grass''', or '''swamp foxtail grass''', is a [[species]] of perennial [[Poaceae|grass]] [[native species|native]] to Asia and Australia. The [[Culm (botany)|culms]] are erect, and 60–100 cm long. The leaf-blades are erect or drooping; flat, or [[wikt:conduplicate|conduplicate]] (folded lengthwise) or [[wikt:involute|involute]] (spiral); and from 10 to 45 cm long by 3–6 mm wide.

The Latin [[specific epithet]] ''alopecuroides'' means "like the genus ''[[Alopecurus]]'' (foxtail)".<ref name=RHSLG>{{cite book | last=Harrison |first=Lorraine | title=RHS Latin for Gardeners | year=2012 |publisher=Mitchell Beazley | location=United Kingdom | isbn=978-1845337315 }}</ref>

==Description==
The plant is a warm season ornamental grass which typically grows in graceful, spreading clumps from {{convert|2-3|ft|m|abbr=on}} tall and wide. It features narrow, medium to deep green leaves (to 1/2" wide) in summer, changing to golden yellow in fall, and fading to beige in late fall. The foliage usually remains attractive throughout the winter. Showy, silvery to pinkish-white, bristly, bottle brush-like flower spikes arch outward from the clump in late summer like water spraying from a fountain (hence the common name "fountain grass"). The flower spikes turn brownish as the seeds form, and usually persist until late fall or early winter before shattering. Many cultivars are available in horticulture, ranging in height from {{convert|1-5 |ft|m|abbr=on}} and featuring a variety of different flower colors (purples, pinks or whites) and autumn foliage.<ref>{{cite web|title=Pennisetum alopecuroides|url=http://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=285289&isprofile=0&letter=P|website=Missouri Botanical Gardens|accessdate=10 November 2016}}</ref>

==Growing conditions==
The plant generally needs a sheltered position in full sun to light shade. It prefers moist, well-drained soil. It will grow in any mild or coastal area where the temperature does not fall below {{convert|-5|C|F|abbr=on}}.<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/43920/Pennisetum-alopecuroides/Details | title = ''Pennisetum alopecuroides'' | website = www.rhs.org | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 24 January 2021}}</ref> The best time of the year for planting is between late Summer and Winter.<ref>{{cite web|title=Pennisetum alopecuroides - Fountain Grass|url=http://www.bluestem.ca/pennisetum-alopec.htm|website=Bluestem|accessdate=10 November 2016}}</ref>

==Cultivars==
The following [[cultivar]]s have received gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]]:
*'Cassian's Choice'<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/154652/Pennisetum-alopecuroides-Cassian-s-Choice/Details | title = ''Pennisetum alopecuroides'' 'Cassian's Choice' | publisher = RHS | access-date = 18 January 2021}}</ref> (brown flowerheads flushed pink)
*'Hameln' <ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/43921/Pennisetum-alopecuroides-Hameln/Details | title = ''Pennisetum alopecuroides'' 'Hameln' | publisher = RHS | access-date = 18 January 2021}}</ref> (purplish flower heads)
*'Red Head' <ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/269612/Pennisetum-alopecuroides-Red-Head/Details | title = ''Pennisetum alopecuroides'' 'Red Head' | publisher = RHS | access-date = 18 January 2021}}</ref> (dark red flower heads)
